"""Liquidity-relaxation repair after a completed high-participation shock.

Mechanism: a sector-relative displacement is more plausibly temporary inventory
transfer when joint range and turnover were elevated but are now cooling.
Liquidity providers can unwind residual hedges after participation subsides,
producing repair in the idiosyncratic component of the prior move.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import rank
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _sector_sum(values: pd.DataFrame, labels: pd.Series) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Broadcast contemporaneous sector sums to each constituent."""
    return values.T.groupby(labels, sort=False).transform("sum").T


@register_factor
class LiquidityRelaxationElasticityRepair(BaseFactor):
    factor_id = "liquidity_relaxation_elasticity_repair"
    name = "Liquidity Relaxation Elasticity Repair"
    category = "microstructure"
    description = (
        "Fade a three-bar leave-one-out sector return displacement only after "
        "a prior joint range-volume shock has demonstrably relaxed."
    )
    window_length = 45
    inputs = ["close", "high", "low", "volume", "sector"]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"]
        high = data["high"].reindex(index=close.index, columns=close.columns)
        low = data["low"].reindex(index=close.index, columns=close.columns)
        volume = data["volume"].reindex(index=close.index, columns=close.columns)

        sector_frame = data["sector"].reindex(index=close.index, columns=close.columns)
        fallback = pd.Series(close.columns, index=close.columns, dtype=object)
        labels = sector_frame.iloc[0].where(sector_frame.iloc[0].notna(), fallback).astype(str)

        safe_close = close.abs().replace(0.0, np.nan)
        bar_range = ((high - low).abs() / safe_close).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        log_range = np.log(bar_range.replace(0.0, np.nan))
        log_volume = np.log(volume.where(volume > 0.0))

        range_base = log_range.rolling(45, min_periods=20).mean()
        volume_base = log_volume.rolling(45, min_periods=20).mean()
        range_abnormal = (log_range - range_base).clip(-3.0, 3.0)
        volume_abnormal = (log_volume - volume_base).clip(-3.0, 3.0)

        # Joint elevation is harder for an isolated stale print to trigger than
        # either range or volume alone.  It is an observable daily proxy for a
        # genuine high-participation liquidity episode.
        joint_shock = np.minimum(range_abnormal, volume_abnormal).clip(lower=0.0).fillna(0.0)
        current_intensity = joint_shock.rolling(3, min_periods=2).mean()
        prior_intensity = joint_shock.shift(3).rolling(3, min_periods=2).mean()
        relaxation = (prior_intensity - current_intensity).clip(lower=0.0)
        prior_gate = prior_intensity / (prior_intensity + 0.35)
        cooling_gate = relaxation / (relaxation + 0.20)
        completed_shock = (prior_gate * cooling_gate).fillna(0.0)

        three_bar_return = (close / close.shift(3) - 1.0).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        valid = three_bar_return.notna().astype(float)
        filled_return = three_bar_return.fillna(0.0)
        sector_sum = _sector_sum(filled_return, labels)
        sector_count = _sector_sum(valid, labels)
        peer_return = (sector_sum - filled_return) / (sector_count - 1.0).replace(0.0, np.nan)
        residual_move = (three_bar_return - peer_return).where(sector_count > 1.0)

        repair = -residual_move.clip(-0.35, 0.35)
        signal = (rank(repair).fillna(0.5) - 0.5) * completed_shock
        return signal.where(three_bar_return.notna(), 0.0).fillna(0.0)
programs.name: Liquidity Relaxation Elasticity Repair
programs.trading_idea: A large sector-relative price displacement is more likely to be a temporary inventory-transfer effect when an earlier joint range-and-turnover shock is now measurably cooling, rather than still accelerating as under information-driven repricing. Dealers and institutional liquidity suppliers unwind residual hedges gradually after participation subsides, creating a short-horizon repair in the stock-specific component of the move; the conditioning on shock relaxation is intended to avoid fading active information events. The hypothesis is falsified if stocks with the largest residual moves after jointly elevated liquidity shocks continue moving in the same direction while range and turnover normalize.
programs.description: The signal measures a stock's three-bar return relative to its leave-one-out sector return, fades that residual move, and activates only after a previously elevated joint range-volume shock has declined. It cross-sectionally ranks the gated repair signal.

programs.code:
"""State-dependent polarity between forced-flow repair and liquidity-vacuum continuation.

Mechanism: sector-wide synchronized range and turnover with mixed return signs
indicates forced risk transfer, for which sector-relative displacements usually
repair.  A strong directional low-volume first-passage asymmetry identifies the
exception: local thin-side depth evacuation, where the same displacement should
continue rather than mean-revert.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import rank
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _sector_mean(values: pd.DataFrame, labels: pd.Series) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Broadcast contemporaneous sector means to each constituent."""
    return values.T.groupby(labels, sort=False).transform("mean").T


def _sector_sum(values: pd.DataFrame, labels: pd.Series) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Broadcast contemporaneous sector sums to each constituent."""
    return values.T.groupby(labels, sort=False).transform("sum").T


def _first_passage_vacuum(
    close: pd.DataFrame,
    high: pd.DataFrame,
    low: pd.DataFrame,
    volume: pd.DataFrame,
    lookback: int,
    barrier: float,
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Signed causal volume-clock barrier-crossing asymmetry.

    Positive values mean that the current directional path reached its barrier
    more cheaply in normalized volume than the opposite directional path.
    """
    safe_close = close.astype(float)
    raw_range = (high.astype(float) - low.astype(float)).abs()
    range_fraction = raw_range / safe_close.abs().replace(0.0, np.nan)
    range_scale = range_fraction.rolling(16, min_periods=6).median()
    range_scale = range_scale.where(range_scale > 0.0)

    ret = safe_close.pct_change(fill_method=None)
    increments = (ret / range_scale).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).fillna(0.0)

    safe_volume = volume.astype(float).clip(lower=0.0).fillna(0.0)
    typical_volume = safe_volume.rolling(16, min_periods=6).median()
    clock_volume = (
        safe_volume / typical_volume.replace(0.0, np.nan)
    ).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).fillna(0.0)

    close_location = (
        (2.0 * safe_close - high.astype(float) - low.astype(float))
        / raw_range.replace(0.0, np.nan)
    ).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).clip(-1.0, 1.0).fillna(0.0)

    increment_array = increments.to_numpy(dtype=float)
    volume_array = clock_volume.to_numpy(dtype=float)
    location_array = close_location.to_numpy(dtype=float)
    n_rows, n_cols = increment_array.shape
    output = np.zeros((n_rows, n_cols), dtype=float)
    columns = np.arange(n_cols)

    for end in range(lookback - 1, n_rows):
        start = end - lookback + 1
        displacement = np.cumsum(increment_array[start : end + 1], axis=0)
        cumulative_volume = np.cumsum(volume_array[start : end + 1], axis=0)

        positive_hit = displacement >= barrier
        negative_hit = displacement <= -barrier
        has_positive = positive_hit.any(axis=0)
        has_negative = negative_hit.any(axis=0)

        first_positive = positive_hit.argmax(axis=0)
        first_negative = negative_hit.argmax(axis=0)
        positive_cost = cumulative_volume[first_positive, columns]
        negative_cost = cumulative_volume[first_negative, columns]
        positive_cost = np.where(has_positive, positive_cost, np.nan)
        negative_cost = np.where(has_negative, negative_cost, np.nan)

        direction = np.sign(displacement[-1])
        own_cost = np.where(direction > 0.0, positive_cost, negative_cost)
        opposite_cost = np.where(direction > 0.0, negative_cost, positive_cost)
        asymmetry = (opposite_cost - own_cost) / (opposite_cost + own_cost)
        asymmetry = np.where(np.isfinite(asymmetry), asymmetry, 0.0)

        endpoint_confirmation = np.maximum(direction * location_array[end], 0.0)
        output[end] = direction * asymmetry * endpoint_confirmation

    return pd.DataFrame(output, index=close.index, columns=close.columns)


@register_factor
class SectorForcedFlowVacuumPolaritySwitch(BaseFactor):
    factor_id = "sector_forcedflow_vacuum_polarity_switch"
    name = "Sector Forced-Flow Vacuum Polarity Switch"
    category = "microstructure"
    description = (
        "Within synchronized, directionally incoherent sector liquidity shocks, "
        "fade sector-relative returns unless a strong low-volume directional "
        "barrier crossing identifies a thin-side vacuum, in which case follow it."
    )
    window_length = 20
    inputs = ["close", "high", "low", "volume", "sector"]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"].astype(float)
        high = data["high"].reindex(index=close.index, columns=close.columns).astype(float)
        low = data["low"].reindex(index=close.index, columns=close.columns).astype(float)
        volume = data["volume"].reindex(index=close.index, columns=close.columns).astype(float)

        sector_frame = data["sector"].reindex(index=close.index, columns=close.columns)
        fallback = pd.Series(close.columns, index=close.columns, dtype=object)
        labels = sector_frame.iloc[0].where(sector_frame.iloc[0].notna(), fallback).astype(str)

        safe_close = close.abs().replace(0.0, np.nan)
        intraday_range = ((high - low).abs() / safe_close).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        log_range = np.log(intraday_range.replace(0.0, np.nan))
        range_abnormal = (
            log_range - log_range.rolling(20, min_periods=10).mean()
        ).clip(-3.0, 3.0).fillna(0.0)

        log_volume = np.log(volume.where(volume > 0.0))
        volume_abnormal = (
            log_volume - log_volume.rolling(20, min_periods=10).mean()
        ).clip(-3.0, 3.0).fillna(0.0)

        range_mean = _sector_mean(range_abnormal, labels)
        volume_mean = _sector_mean(volume_abnormal, labels)
        range_dispersion = np.sqrt(
            _sector_mean((range_abnormal - range_mean).pow(2.0), labels).clip(lower=0.0)
        )
        volume_dispersion = np.sqrt(
            _sector_mean((volume_abnormal - volume_mean).pow(2.0), labels).clip(lower=0.0)
        )
        common_shock = range_mean.combine(volume_mean, np.minimum).clip(lower=0.0)
        liquidity_sync = common_shock / (1.0 + range_dispersion + volume_dispersion)

        raw_return = close.pct_change(fill_method=None).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        clipped_return = raw_return.clip(-1.0, 1.0)
        valid = clipped_return.notna().astype(float)
        grouped_return = clipped_return.fillna(0.0)
        sector_sum = _sector_sum(grouped_return, labels)
        sector_count = _sector_sum(valid, labels)
        leave_one_out = (sector_sum - grouped_return) / (sector_count - 1.0)
        leave_one_out = leave_one_out.where(sector_count > 1.0)
        return_deviation = (clipped_return - leave_one_out).fillna(0.0)

        sign_sum = _sector_sum(np.sign(grouped_return), labels)
        sign_coherence = (sign_sum / sector_count.replace(0.0, np.nan)).abs()
        sign_coherence = sign_coherence.where(sector_count > 0.0, 1.0).clip(0.0, 1.0)
        event_strength = liquidity_sync / (liquidity_sync + 0.10)
        forced_flow_event = event_strength * (1.0 - sign_coherence).pow(2.0)

        repair = (-return_deviation / (1.0 + volume_abnormal.clip(lower=0.0))).clip(-1.0, 1.0)
        vacuum = _first_passage_vacuum(close, high, low, volume, 14, 1.5).clip(-1.0, 1.0)

        # This is a polarity selection, not an averaging rule: only an endpoint-
        # confirmed, volume-efficient barrier crossing overturns the forced-flow fade.
        confirmed_vacuum = vacuum.abs() >= 0.35
        selected_response = repair.where(~confirmed_vacuum, vacuum)
        signal = (rank(selected_response).fillna(0.5) - 0.5) * forced_flow_event
        return signal.where(raw_return.notna(), 0.0).fillna(0.0)
programs.name: Sector Forced-Flow Vacuum Polarity Switch
programs.trading_idea: A synchronized sector-wide range-and-turnover shock with mixed return signs is usually forced risk transfer, so an ordinary sector-relative displacement should mean-revert. However, if the displaced name also reached its directional range barrier on unusually little volume relative to the opposite direction, the move is more consistent with a name-specific thin-side liquidity vacuum than temporary portfolio rebalancing, and the correct response switches to continuation. This interaction separates reversible sector inventory redistribution from locally depleted depth, a distinction neither unconditional sector fading nor unconditional volume-clock continuation can make alone.
programs.description: During sector-synchronized but directionally incoherent liquidity events, the factor normally fades a stock's leave-one-out sector return deviation. It switches to following the directional volume-clock first-passage signal only when that stock's excursion has a sufficiently strong low-volume barrier-crossing asymmetry.

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import indneutralize, rank
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _zscore(values: pd.DataFrame, window: int) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Causal trailing standardisation requiring a complete trailing history."""
    mean = values.rolling(window, min_periods=window).mean()
    std = values.rolling(window, min_periods=window).std()
    return (values - mean) / std.replace(0.0, np.nan)


def _decaying_stress(
    impact: pd.DataFrame,
    volume_innovation: pd.DataFrame,
    window: int,
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Identify a past stress peak followed by declining impact and participation.

    All statistics are trailing. A large positive value means a recent impact
    shock occurred, while both its current level and volume innovation have
    subsequently cooled, consistent with passive-liquidity replenishment.
    """
    prior_peak = impact.shift(1).rolling(window, min_periods=window).max()
    impact_decay = (prior_peak - impact).clip(lower=0.0)
    volume_cooling = (-volume_innovation).clip(lower=0.0)
    return prior_peak.clip(lower=0.0) * impact_decay * volume_cooling


@register_factor
class LiquidityRefillDecayAsymmetry(BaseFactor):
    """Fade directional moves after a temporary impact shock visibly cools."""

    factor_id = "liquidity_refill_decay_asymmetry"
    name = "Liquidity Refill Decay Asymmetry"
    category = "microstructure"
    description = (
        "Contrarian sector-residual return signal activated when a recent "
        "range-per-volume impact shock is followed by declining impact and "
        "cooling volume participation, indicating liquidity replenishment."
    )
    window_length = 65
    inputs = ["close", "high", "low", "volume", "sector"]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"].replace(0.0, np.nan)
        high = data["high"]
        low = data["low"]
        volume = data["volume"].clip(lower=0.0)

        ret = close.pct_change(fill_method=None)
        prior_close = close.shift(1)
        true_range = (high - low).abs() / prior_close

        dollar_volume = (close * volume).replace(0.0, np.nan)
        impact = true_range / dollar_volume
        log_impact = np.log1p(impact.clip(lower=0.0))
        impact_z = _zscore(log_impact, 60)

        log_volume = np.log1p(volume)
        volume_innovation = _zscore(log_volume.diff(), 60)
        refill = _decaying_stress(impact_z, volume_innovation, 5)

        recent_return = ret.rolling(5, min_periods=5).sum()
        sector_residual = indneutralize(recent_return, data["sector"])

        raw_signal = -sector_residual * refill
        raw_signal = raw_signal.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        return rank(raw_signal).fillna(0.5)

programs.trading_idea: The parent’s delayed payoff suggests that daily price-leading volume loops are not immediate reversal signals but mark a temporary liquidity deficit whose impact decays as passive liquidity refills. This child measures whether abnormal range and participation are subsiding after a directional shock: a same-direction move with decaying impact and volume is more likely execution overhang and should reverse over the following week, whereas persistent or accelerating stress is more likely informed flow and is excluded. The hypothesis is falsified if decaying post-shock liquidity stress continues to predict same-direction returns after sector demeaning; the edge can persist because inventory replenishment, execution schedules, and slow-moving institutional rebalancing unwind over several sessions rather than intraday.
programs.description: Ranks the contrarian direction of recent sector-residual returns only when a prior price-impact shock is followed by jointly declining abnormal range and volume innovation. It uses an exponentially decayed impact proxy to distinguish replenishing temporary liquidity demand from persistent information-driven participation.

"""Financially resilient, thin-turnover downside dislocations should repair.

Mechanism: a large downside range on unusually little turnover is consistent with a
transient liquidity vacuum rather than broad information discovery.  Conditioning
on cash liquidity and low leverage separates likely forced-flow dislocations from
moves carrying near-term solvency information.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import indneutralize, rank
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _resilience_score(cash_ratio: pd.DataFrame, debt_to_assets: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Conservative cross-sectional balance-sheet buffer using available values only."""
    cash = rank(cash_ratio.where(cash_ratio > 0.0))
    debt = rank((-debt_to_assets).where(debt_to_assets >= 0.0))
    available = cash.notna().astype(float) + debt.notna().astype(float)
    score = (cash.fillna(0.0) + debt.fillna(0.0)) / available.replace(0.0, np.nan)
    return score.fillna(0.0)


@register_factor
class ResilientThinTurnoverLiquidationRepair(BaseFactor):
    factor_id = "resilient_thin_turnover_liquidation_repair"
    name = "Resilient Thin-Turnover Liquidation Repair"
    category = "microstructure"
    description = (
        "Sector-neutral rank of recent downside range shocks that occurred on "
        "low relative turnover, conditioned on cash liquidity and low leverage."
    )
    window_length = 20
    inputs = ["close", "high", "low", "volume", "cashRatio", "debtToAssets", "sector"]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"].astype(float)
        high = data["high"].astype(float)
        low = data["low"].astype(float)
        volume = data["volume"].astype(float)

        safe_close = close.where(close > 0.0)
        daily_range = ((high - low).abs() / safe_close).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        range_base = daily_range.rolling(20, min_periods=20).mean().replace(0.0, np.nan)
        relative_range = daily_range / range_base

        volume_base = volume.where(volume > 0.0).rolling(20, min_periods=20).mean()
        relative_turnover = volume / volume_base.replace(0.0, np.nan)
        thinness = 1.0 / relative_turnover.replace(0.0, np.nan)

        ret = close.pct_change().replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        downside = (-ret).clip(lower=0.0).rolling(3, min_periods=3).sum()
        liquidation_state = rank(downside * relative_range) * rank(thinness)

        resilience = _resilience_score(
            data["cashRatio"].astype(float),
            data["debtToAssets"].astype(float),
        )
        raw_signal = liquidation_state * resilience
        neutral_signal = indneutralize(raw_signal, data["sector"])
        return rank(neutral_signal).reindex(index=close.index, columns=close.columns).fillna(0.0)
programs.name: Resilient Thin-Turnover Liquidation Repair
programs.trading_idea: A downside move accompanied by an unusually large range but unusually low turnover is more consistent with a temporary liquidity vacuum or an urgent, price-insensitive seller than with broad information-driven repricing. The signal only rewards these dislocations in financially resilient firms, where strong cash liquidity and low leverage make immediate solvency news less plausible and therefore make price repair more likely over the next six bars. This is falsifiable: the positive return spread should be concentrated in high-buffer, low-relative-turnover downside shocks and should vanish or reverse for high-turnover shocks or weak-balance-sheet firms. The edge can persist because liquidity providers face inventory, funding, and adverse-selection costs during episodic thin trading, so they do not instantaneously arbitrage away temporary price concessions.
programs.description: Ranks recent downside moves whose percentage range is high relative to the stock's trailing range baseline while volume is low relative to trailing turnover, conditioned on a simple cash-versus-leverage resilience score. The result is sector-neutralized to isolate idiosyncratic liquidation-repair states.

"""Conditional fundamental-delivery translation under a quality-value premium regime.

A delivery-versus-price gap is most actionable when the market is rewarding the
quality and valuation characteristics that validate that delivery.  The regime
premium is estimated only from completed six-bar returns and is used as a
cross-sectional interaction, rather than as an unconditional factor blend.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _groups(industry: pd.DataFrame, columns: pd.Index) -> pd.Series:
    """Stable industry labels, with singleton fallbacks for missing labels."""
    labels = industry.iloc[0].reindex(columns).astype(object)
    fallback = pd.Series(
        ["__singleton_" + str(column) for column in columns],
        index=columns,
        dtype=object,
    )
    return labels.where(labels.notna(), fallback)


def _industry_mean(values: pd.DataFrame, groups: pd.Series) -> pd.DataFrame:
    return values.T.groupby(groups, sort=False).transform("mean").T


def _industry_rank(values: pd.DataFrame, groups: pd.Series) -> pd.DataFrame:
    ranked = values.T.groupby(groups, sort=False).rank(pct=True).T
    return ranked - _industry_mean(ranked, groups)


def _event_mask(values: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """First available observation and subsequent public revisions."""
    prior = values.shift(1)
    return values.notna() & (prior.isna() | values.ne(prior))


def _latest_at_event(values: pd.DataFrame, event: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    return values.where(event).ffill()


def _event_age(event: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    event_array = event.fillna(False).to_numpy(dtype=bool)
    rows, columns = event_array.shape
    positions = np.arange(rows, dtype=float)[:, None]
    last = np.maximum.accumulate(np.where(event_array, positions, -1.0), axis=0)
    age = positions - last
    age[last < 0.0] = np.nan
    return pd.DataFrame(age, index=event.index, columns=event.columns)


def _cs_zscore(values: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    clean = values.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
    center = clean.mean(axis=1)
    spread = clean.std(axis=1, ddof=0).replace(0.0, np.nan)
    return clean.sub(center, axis=0).div(spread, axis=0).clip(-4.0, 4.0).fillna(0.0)


def _quality_value_premium(
    exposure: pd.DataFrame, close: pd.DataFrame
) -> pd.Series:
    """Causal EW payoff estimate for a quality-value sleeve.

    The return ending at t is paired with exposure observed at t-6, so every
    payoff used by the state estimate was fully completed by t.
    """
    completed_return = close.pct_change(6).clip(-0.75, 0.75)
    payoff = exposure.shift(6).mul(completed_return).mean(axis=1)
    premium = payoff.ewm(halflife=42.0, adjust=False, min_periods=30).mean()
    baseline = premium.rolling(126, min_periods=42).mean()
    scale = premium.rolling(126, min_periods=42).std().replace(0.0, np.nan)
    return ((premium - baseline) / scale).clip(-2.0, 2.0)


@register_factor
class ConditionalDeliveryPremiumTranslation(BaseFactor):
    factor_id = "conditional_delivery_premium_translation"
    name = "Conditional Delivery Translation"
    category = "statistical_arbitrage"
    description = (
        "Industry-relative earnings-delivery versus post-update-price gaps, "
        "interacted with a causal realized quality-value premium state."
    )
    window_length = 168
    inputs = [
        "close",
        "industry",
        "epsSurprise",
        "epsEstimate",
        "operatingCashFlow",
        "sharesOutstanding",
        "roic",
        "incomeQuality",
        "earningsYield",
        "freeCashFlowYield",
    ]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"].apply(pd.to_numeric, errors="coerce")
        groups = _groups(data["industry"], close.columns)

        surprise = data["epsSurprise"].apply(pd.to_numeric, errors="coerce")
        estimate = data["epsEstimate"].apply(pd.to_numeric, errors="coerce")
        cash_flow = data["operatingCashFlow"].apply(pd.to_numeric, errors="coerce")
        shares = data["sharesOutstanding"].apply(pd.to_numeric, errors="coerce")

        surprise_event = _event_mask(surprise)
        estimate_event = _event_mask(estimate)
        cash_event = _event_mask(cash_flow)
        shares_event = _event_mask(shares)
        any_event = surprise_event | estimate_event | cash_event | shares_event

        surprise_score = (
            surprise / estimate.abs().replace(0.0, np.nan)
        ).clip(-5.0, 5.0)
        estimate_change = (
            (estimate - estimate.shift(1))
            / estimate.shift(1).abs().replace(0.0, np.nan)
        ).clip(-2.0, 2.0)
        cash_change = (
            (cash_flow - cash_flow.shift(1))
            / cash_flow.shift(1).abs().replace(0.0, np.nan)
        ).clip(-5.0, 5.0)
        dilution_discipline = (
            -(shares - shares.shift(1))
            / shares.shift(1).abs().replace(0.0, np.nan)
        ).clip(-0.5, 0.5)

        components = [
            _industry_rank(_latest_at_event(surprise_score, surprise_event), groups),
            _industry_rank(_latest_at_event(estimate_change, estimate_event), groups),
            _industry_rank(_latest_at_event(cash_change, cash_event), groups),
            _industry_rank(_latest_at_event(dilution_discipline, shares_event), groups),
        ]
        numerator = sum(component.fillna(0.0) for component in components)
        denominator = sum(component.notna().astype(float) for component in components)
        delivery_order = numerator / denominator.replace(0.0, np.nan)

        log_close = np.log(close.where(close > 0.0))
        relative_log_price = log_close - _industry_mean(log_close, groups)
        event_anchor = relative_log_price.where(any_event).ffill()
        post_update_return = relative_log_price - event_anchor
        price_order = _industry_rank(post_update_return, groups)

        age = _event_age(any_event)
        freshness = np.exp(-np.log(2.0) * age / 18.0).where(age <= 63.0, 0.0)
        delivery_gap = (delivery_order - price_order) * freshness

        quality = (_cs_zscore(data["roic"]) + _cs_zscore(data["incomeQuality"])) / 2.0
        value = (
            _cs_zscore(data["earningsYield"])
            + _cs_zscore(data["freeCashFlowYield"])
        ) / 2.0
        quality_value_exposure = ((quality + value) / 2.0).clip(-3.0, 3.0)
        premium_state = _quality_value_premium(quality_value_exposure, close).fillna(0.0)

        # A positive realized premium makes aligned fundamental delivery more
        # credible; a negative premium attenuates, but does not mechanically
        # reverse, the separate delivery-price convergence mechanism.
        multiplier = (
            1.0 + 0.35 * quality_value_exposure.mul(premium_state, axis=0)
        ).clip(0.25, 1.75)
        signal = delivery_gap * multiplier
        signal = signal - _industry_mean(signal, groups)

        return signal.reindex(index=close.index, columns=close.columns).replace(
            [np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan
        ).fillna(0.0).astype(float)

The child estimates a slow, causal realized premium for a conservative profitability/value sleeve, then uses it to amplify delivery-price gaps for firms whose current fundamental exposure is aligned with that regime and suppress gaps when the regime rejects such characteristics. Parent A identifies delayed peer-relative assimilation, while Parent B supplies the state variable distinguishing credible fundamental underreaction from periods in which similar delivery news is discounted.

"""Delivery-conditioned estimate revisions with an immediate price-assimilation gate.

Mechanism: a forecast update is directional only when cash realization and
working-capital delivery validate it.  The market's initial industry-relative
price response determines whether that validated information remains unpriced
at the six-bar horizon.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import indneutralize, rank
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _revision_zscore(level: pd.DataFrame, window: int) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Causal standardized innovation for a point-in-time estimate series."""
    clean = level.astype(float)
    scale = clean.abs().rolling(window, min_periods=20).median()
    innovation = clean.diff() / scale.replace(0.0, np.nan)
    mean = innovation.rolling(window, min_periods=20).mean()
    std = innovation.rolling(window, min_periods=20).std()
    return ((innovation - mean) / std.replace(0.0, np.nan)).clip(-5.0, 5.0)


def _quarterly_relative_change(frame: pd.DataFrame, lag: int) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Causal disclosed-quarter change, robust to differing accounting scales."""
    prior = frame.astype(float).shift(lag)
    return (frame.astype(float) - prior) / prior.abs().replace(0.0, np.nan)


def _cs_center(frame: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Cross-sectional robust centering; absent accounting data is neutral."""
    return rank(frame.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)).fillna(0.5) - 0.5


@register_factor
class RevisionDeliveryResponseDeficit(BaseFactor):
    factor_id = "revision_delivery_response_deficit"
    name = "Revision Delivery Response Deficit"
    category = "momentum"
    description = (
        "Fresh consensus revisions are multiplied by cash-delivery credibility "
        "and gated by the absence of an already-confirming industry-relative "
        "two-bar price response."
    )
    window_length = 126
    inputs = [
        "close",
        "industry",
        "epsEstimate",
        "revenueEstimate",
        "incomeQuality",
        "receivablesGrowth",
        "inventoryGrowth",
        "cashConversionCycle",
        "operatingCashFlowGrowth",
        "sharesGrowth",
    ]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"].astype(float)
        industry = data["industry"]
        eps_estimate = data["epsEstimate"].astype(float)
        revenue_estimate = data["revenueEstimate"].astype(float)

        eps_revision = _revision_zscore(eps_estimate, 126)
        revenue_revision = _revision_zscore(revenue_estimate, 126)
        revision = (0.65 * eps_revision.fillna(0.0) + 0.35 * revenue_revision.fillna(0.0)).clip(-5.0, 5.0)

        # Estimate fields are step functions: trade only a genuinely fresh update,
        # rather than the stale z-score left between report dates.
        fresh = eps_estimate.diff().abs().gt(0.0) | revenue_estimate.diff().abs().gt(0.0)

        cash_cycle_change = _quarterly_relative_change(data["cashConversionCycle"], 63)
        delivery = (
            0.30 * _cs_center(data["incomeQuality"].astype(float).clip(-3.0, 3.0))
            + 0.20 * _cs_center(-data["receivablesGrowth"].astype(float).clip(-3.0, 3.0))
            + 0.15 * _cs_center(-data["inventoryGrowth"].astype(float).clip(-3.0, 3.0))
            + 0.20 * _cs_center(-cash_cycle_change.clip(-3.0, 3.0))
            + 0.10 * _cs_center(data["operatingCashFlowGrowth"].astype(float).clip(-3.0, 3.0))
            + 0.05 * _cs_center(-data["sharesGrowth"].astype(float).clip(-1.0, 1.0))
        ).clip(-0.5, 0.5)

        # A response aligned with the new forecast means the information has
        # already been assimilated.  Neutral or opposing relative response keeps
        # the delivery-conditioned forecast signal active.
        two_bar_return = close.pct_change(2)
        industry_residual = indneutralize(two_bar_return, industry).fillna(0.0)
        response_vol = industry_residual.rolling(20, min_periods=10).std()
        direction = np.sign(revision)
        aligned_response = (direction * industry_residual / response_vol.replace(0.0, np.nan)).clip(-4.0, 4.0)
        underreaction_gate = (2.0 / (1.0 + np.exp(aligned_response))).fillna(1.0)

        score = (revision * delivery * underreaction_gate).where(fresh, 0.0)
        signal = rank(score.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)).fillna(0.5)
        return signal.reindex(index=close.index, columns=close.columns).astype(float)
programs.name: Revision Delivery Response Deficit
programs.trading_idea: Consensus revisions should persist only when the underlying delivery state is credible: strong cash conversion and income quality, with receivables, inventory, and dilution not signaling that reported growth is being financed rather than realized. The child trades this delivery-conditioned revision only when the stock has not yet made an industry-relative price response in the revision direction, concentrating the signal on the short-lived assimilation gap relevant to six bars. Neither parent alone distinguishes a credible versus fragile revision from whether that information has already been incorporated into relative prices; their interaction isolates unpriced, economically validated forecast news.
programs.description: The signal multiplies fresh EPS/revenue consensus innovations by a cross-sectional cash-delivery credibility score, then suppresses revisions whose two-bar industry-relative price response has already confirmed the news. Weak delivery reverses the revision sign, while credible but unassimilated revisions receive the largest directional scores.

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import rank
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _relative_revision(level: pd.DataFrame, window: int) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Scale a fresh point-in-time consensus change by its trailing level."""
    x = level.astype(float)
    scale = x.abs().rolling(window, min_periods=20).median().replace(0.0, np.nan)
    return (x.diff() / scale).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)


def _industry_relative_return(ret: pd.DataFrame, industry: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Subtract the contemporaneous static-industry return, causally by row."""
    labels = industry.iloc[0].copy()
    labels = labels.fillna("__unknown__")
    peer_mean = ret.T.groupby(labels).transform("mean").T
    return ret - peer_mean


@register_factor
class LowAttentionRevisionTranslationLag(BaseFactor):
    """Fresh consensus news whose price translation is delayed by low attention."""

    factor_id = "low_attention_revision_translation_lag"
    name = "Low-Attention Revision Translation Lag"
    category = "momentum"
    description = (
        "Fresh EPS and revenue estimate revisions weighted by low relative volume "
        "and an insufficient same-day industry-relative price response."
    )
    window_length = 126
    inputs = ["close", "volume", "epsEstimate", "revenueEstimate", "industry"]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"].astype(float)
        volume = data["volume"].astype(float)

        eps_rev = _relative_revision(data["epsEstimate"], 126)
        revenue_rev = _relative_revision(data["revenueEstimate"], 126)
        revision = (0.7 * eps_rev.fillna(0.0) + 0.3 * revenue_rev.fillna(0.0)).clip(-2.0, 2.0)
        fresh = (eps_rev.notna() & eps_rev.ne(0.0)) | (revenue_rev.notna() & revenue_rev.ne(0.0))

        direction = np.sign(revision)
        magnitude = rank(revision.abs()).fillna(0.5)

        ret = close.pct_change()
        industry_ret = _industry_relative_return(ret, data["industry"])
        vol = ret.rolling(21, min_periods=10).std().replace(0.0, np.nan)
        response_z = industry_ret / vol
        aligned_response = direction * response_z
        translation_lag = (1.0 - aligned_response).clip(0.0, 2.0)

        relative_volume = volume / volume.rolling(21, min_periods=10).mean().replace(0.0, np.nan)
        low_attention = 1.0 - rank(relative_volume).fillna(0.5)

        score = direction * magnitude * translation_lag * low_attention
        score = score.where(fresh, 0.0)
        return rank(score.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)).fillna(0.5)
programs.name: Low-Attention Revision Translation Lag
programs.trading_idea: Fresh analyst-consensus revisions should predict near-term returns only when the market has not already translated the news into price. A revision released during unusually low trading participation, with a muted or opposite same-day industry-relative price response, indicates incomplete attention and slow institutional rebalancing rather than a fully assimilated update. The edge can persist because arbitrageurs face sparse, heterogeneous revision events and cannot cheaply distinguish temporarily ignored revisions from low-quality news without bearing event and model risk.
programs.description: Ranks fresh EPS and revenue estimate changes by their magnitude, then weights them by low relative volume and the shortfall of same-day industry-relative price response in the revision direction. Positive unassimilated upgrades score high, while unassimilated downgrades score low.

"""Failed fragile-firm sell cascades absorbed above a VWAP cost-basis anchor."""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import rank
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _fragility_score(
    cash_ratio: pd.DataFrame,
    debt_to_capital: pd.DataFrame,
    net_debt_to_ebitda: pd.DataFrame,
    interest_coverage: pd.DataFrame,
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Robust cross-sectional balance-sheet fragility score."""
    def _clean_rank(frame: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
        clean = frame.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        return clean.rank(axis=1, pct=True).fillna(0.5)

    low_cash = 1.0 - _clean_rank(cash_ratio)
    high_debt = _clean_rank(debt_to_capital)
    high_net_debt = _clean_rank(net_debt_to_ebitda)
    low_coverage = 1.0 - _clean_rank(interest_coverage)
    return (low_cash + high_debt + high_net_debt + low_coverage) / 4.0


def _sell_excitation(
    close: pd.DataFrame,
    open_: pd.DataFrame,
    volume: pd.DataFrame,
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Causal exponential sell-event intensity relative to its trailing norm."""
    baseline_volume = volume.rolling(20, min_periods=10).mean().replace(0.0, np.nan)
    relative_volume = (volume / baseline_volume).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
    relative_volume = relative_volume.fillna(0.0).clip(lower=0.0, upper=10.0)

    direction = np.sign((close - open_).fillna(0.0))
    sell_events = (-direction * relative_volume).clip(lower=0.0)
    alpha = 0.15
    intensity = sell_events.ewm(alpha=alpha, adjust=False).mean() / alpha
    baseline = intensity.rolling(60, min_periods=30).mean().replace(0.0, np.nan)
    excess = (intensity / baseline - 1.0).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
    return excess.clip(lower=0.0).fillna(0.0)


@register_factor
class FragileSupplyAbsorptionVwapEscape(BaseFactor):
    """High fragile sell excitation that fails to break an accepted VWAP anchor."""

    factor_id = "fragile_supply_absorption_vwap_escape"
    name = "Fragile Supply Absorption VWAP Escape"
    category = "microstructure"
    description = (
        "Ranks financially fragile names whose abnormal sell-flow excitation is "
        "absorbed while price and volume participation remain above a rolling VWAP."
    )
    window_length = 60
    inputs = [
        "close",
        "open",
        "volume",
        "cashRatio",
        "debtToCapital",
        "netDebtToEbitda",
        "interestCoverage",
    ]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"].replace(0.0, np.nan)
        open_ = data["open"].replace(0.0, np.nan)
        volume = data["volume"].fillna(0.0).clip(lower=0.0)

        valid_volume = volume.where(close.notna(), 0.0)
        vwap_denominator = valid_volume.rolling(40, min_periods=20).sum()
        reference_vwap = (
            (close * valid_volume).fillna(0.0).rolling(40, min_periods=20).sum()
            / vwap_denominator.replace(0.0, np.nan)
        )
        displacement = close / reference_vwap.replace(0.0, np.nan) - 1.0

        above_volume = volume.where(displacement > 0.0, 0.0)
        above_participation = (
            above_volume.rolling(10, min_periods=5).sum()
            / volume.rolling(10, min_periods=5).sum().replace(0.0, np.nan)
        )
        participation_lift = (
            volume.rolling(10, min_periods=5).mean()
            / volume.rolling(40, min_periods=20).mean().replace(0.0, np.nan)
        ).clip(lower=0.0, upper=5.0)
        accepted_flow = (above_participation * participation_lift).replace(
            [np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan
        )

        fragility = _fragility_score(
            data["cashRatio"],
            data["debtToCapital"],
            data["netDebtToEbitda"],
            data["interestCoverage"],
        )
        sell_excitation = _sell_excitation(close, open_, volume)
        failed_cascade = sell_excitation * fragility

        composite = (
            rank(displacement).fillna(0.5)
            + rank(accepted_flow).fillna(0.5)
            + rank(failed_cascade).fillna(0.5)
        )
        composite = composite.where(displacement > 0.0, -1.0)
        return rank(composite).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).fillna(0.5)
programs.name: Fragile Supply Absorption VWAP Escape
programs.trading_idea: A financially fragile issuer experiencing a self-exciting sequence of high-volume sell bars would normally suffer continuing forced-risk-reduction pressure. If that sell cascade instead occurs while price remains persistently above its volume-weighted cost-basis proxy and above-anchor participation stays high, marginal forced supply is being absorbed without restoring price pressure. This interaction identifies a failed downside cascade and supply-exhaustion transition: Parent B supplies the latent forced-selling test, while Parent A identifies that the market has accepted that flow above the holder reference point, creating a short-horizon upside continuation neither condition establishes alone.
programs.description: The signal ranks fragile firms with unusually elevated exponentially decayed sell-flow intensity, conditional on positive displacement from a trailing VWAP and sustained above-reference volume participation. It is high only where an apparent forced-selling cascade is absorbed rather than allowed to break the reference-price anchor.

"""Reference-point terminal rejection after failed high-volume acceptance.

Mechanism: trading above a rolling VWAP cost-basis proxy normally tests latent
holder supply.  When turnover is elevated but a substantial intrabar excursion
above that reference closes near the daily low, the apparent acceptance was
terminal demand exhaustion rather than durable supply absorption.  Such failed
acceptance should unwind over the subsequent week as residual reference-point
sellers distribute inventory.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import rank
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _rolling_reference_vwap(
    close: pd.DataFrame, volume: pd.DataFrame, window: int
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Causal rolling VWAP proxy for the aggregate recent holder cost basis."""
    valid_volume = volume.where(close.notna(), 0.0)
    notional = (close * valid_volume).fillna(0.0)
    total_volume = valid_volume.rolling(window, min_periods=window // 2).sum()
    return notional.rolling(window, min_periods=window // 2).sum() / total_volume.replace(0.0, np.nan)


@register_factor
class ReferencePointTerminalRejection(BaseFactor):
    factor_id = "reference_point_terminal_rejection"
    name = "Reference-Point Terminal Rejection"
    category = "microstructure"
    description = (
        "High-volume failed acceptance above a rolling VWAP reference: ranks "
        "large above-reference excursions that close near the daily low."
    )
    window_length = 40
    inputs = ["high", "low", "close", "volume"]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"].replace(0.0, np.nan)
        high = data["high"].replace(0.0, np.nan)
        low = data["low"].replace(0.0, np.nan)
        volume = data["volume"].fillna(0.0).clip(lower=0.0)

        reference = _rolling_reference_vwap(close, volume, 40)
        displacement = close / reference.replace(0.0, np.nan) - 1.0
        high_extension = high / reference.replace(0.0, np.nan) - 1.0

        daily_range = (high - low).replace(0.0, np.nan)
        close_to_low_rejection = ((high - close) / daily_range).clip(lower=0.0, upper=1.0)

        short_volume = volume.rolling(5, min_periods=3).mean()
        long_volume = volume.rolling(40, min_periods=20).mean()
        turnover_pressure = (short_volume / long_volume.replace(0.0, np.nan)).clip(lower=0.0, upper=5.0)

        # The event is meaningful only if the close still remains above the
        # reference while the bar demonstrates a failed attempt to hold a
        # further above-reference extension.
        accepted_then_rejected = (displacement > 0.0) & (high_extension > 0.0)
        rejection_intensity = close_to_low_rejection * high_extension.clip(lower=0.0)

        composite = (
            rank(displacement.clip(lower=0.0)).fillna(0.5)
            + rank(turnover_pressure).fillna(0.5)
            + rank(rejection_intensity).fillna(0.5)
        )
        composite = composite.where(accepted_then_rejected, -1.0)
        return rank(composite).fillna(0.5)
programs.name: Reference-Point Terminal Rejection
programs.trading_idea: A high-volume move above a rolling volume-weighted cost-basis proxy can initially look like supply absorption, but a close near the day’s low after a large above-reference excursion identifies terminal rejection: marginal buyers were willing to transact at elevated prices but could not retain control into the close. This is a conditioned reference-point mechanism rather than a generic reversal signal, because the rejection is informative only when turnover is elevated and the stock remains above its aggregate cost-basis proxy. The edge should persist because latent holder cost bases, dispersed supply, and the distinction between apparent acceptance and failed acceptance are difficult to infer and arbitrage from daily bars; it is falsified if high-scoring names outperform rather than underperform over the next six sessions.

"""Recovery-confirmed exhaustion of self-exciting downside volatility."""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import rank
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _recovery_confirmed_exhaustion(
    close: pd.DataFrame, high: pd.DataFrame, low: pd.DataFrame
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Causal interaction of downside-shock absorption and excitation cooling."""
    safe_close = close.where(close > 0.0)
    ret = safe_close.pct_change(fill_method=None)
    ret = ret.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).clip(lower=-0.95, upper=5.0)

    downside_sq = (-ret.clip(upper=0.0)).pow(2).fillna(0.0)
    prior_variance = ret.pow(2).rolling(40, min_periods=20).mean().shift(1)
    prior_variance = prior_variance.clip(lower=1.0e-10)
    innovation = (downside_sq / prior_variance).replace(
        [np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan
    ).clip(lower=0.0, upper=25.0).fillna(0.0)

    intensity = innovation.ewm(halflife=2.0, adjust=False, min_periods=3).mean()
    intensity = intensity.fillna(0.0)
    intensity_mean = intensity.rolling(30, min_periods=15).mean().shift(1)
    intensity_std = intensity.rolling(30, min_periods=15).std().shift(1)
    burst = ((intensity - intensity_mean) / intensity_std.replace(0.0, np.nan))
    burst = burst.clip(lower=0.0, upper=5.0).fillna(0.0)

    curvature = intensity - 2.0 * intensity.shift(1) + intensity.shift(2)
    curvature_scale = curvature.rolling(30, min_periods=15).std().shift(1)
    cooling = (-curvature / curvature_scale.replace(0.0, np.nan))
    cooling = cooling.clip(lower=0.0, upper=5.0).fillna(0.0)

    bar_range = (high - low).where((high - low) > 0.0)
    recovery = ((close - low) / bar_range).clip(lower=0.0, upper=1.0).fillna(0.5)

    return innovation * burst * cooling * recovery

class RecoveryConfirmedExcitationExhaustion(BaseFactor):

"""Disclosure liquidation cooling repair: buy exhausted bad-news selling.

Mechanism: negative disclosures can trigger forced deleveraging and asymmetric
sell-side liquidity withdrawal in financially fragile firms.  A rebound is most
likely after a clustered downside price-volume pressure state begins to cool
while the bar closes away from its low, revealing that marginal selling has
been absorbed rather than that information is still being incorporated.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import rank
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _fresh_update(values: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Identify newly available point-in-time quarterly observations causally."""
    clean = values.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
    prior = clean.shift(1)
    return clean.notna() & (prior.isna() | clean.ne(prior))


def _decayed_event_state(event_score: pd.DataFrame, halflife: float) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Causal exponential event kernel; zero non-events decay prior news."""
    return event_score.fillna(0.0).ewm(
        halflife=halflife, adjust=False, min_periods=1
    ).mean()


def _downside_liquidation_cooling(
    close: pd.DataFrame,
    high: pd.DataFrame,
    low: pd.DataFrame,
    volume: pd.DataFrame,
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Bounded proxy for a cooling self-exciting downside liquidation episode.

    Downside standardized returns marked by abnormal volume proxy sell-pressure
    arrivals.  Their exponentially decayed intensity is high after a cluster;
    cooling compares today's arrival to yesterday's inherited intensity.  All
    rolling and decay operations use information available at the current bar.
    """
    ret = close.pct_change().replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
    ret_scale = ret.rolling(20, min_periods=12).std().replace(0.0, np.nan)
    downside = (-ret / ret_scale).clip(lower=0.0, upper=3.0).fillna(0.0) / 3.0

    vol_mean = volume.rolling(20, min_periods=12).mean()
    vol_std = volume.rolling(20, min_periods=12).std().replace(0.0, np.nan)
    activity = ((volume - vol_mean) / vol_std).clip(lower=0.0, upper=3.0).fillna(0.0)
    marked_arrival = downside * activity
    intensity = marked_arrival.ewm(halflife=3.0, adjust=False, min_periods=1).mean()
    inherited = intensity.shift(1).fillna(0.0)

    cooling = (1.0 - marked_arrival / inherited.replace(0.0, np.nan)).clip(0.0, 1.0)
    cooling = cooling.where(inherited.gt(0.0), 0.0).fillna(0.0)
    pressure = (inherited / 3.0).clip(0.0, 1.0)

    bar_range = (high - low).replace(0.0, np.nan)
    close_location = ((close - low) / bar_range).clip(0.0, 1.0).fillna(0.5)
    rejection = ((close_location - 0.5) * 2.0).clip(0.0, 1.0)
    return (pressure * cooling * rejection).clip(0.0, 1.0)


@register_factor
class DisclosureLiquidationCoolingRepair(BaseFactor):
    factor_id = "disclosure_liquidation_cooling_repair"
    name = "Disclosure Liquidation Cooling Repair"
    category = "microstructure"
    description = (
        "Long score for financially fragile firms with a fresh negative earnings "
        "or revenue disclosure whose abnormal downside price-volume pressure is "
        "cooling and whose bar rejects the intraday low."
    )
    window_length = 60
    inputs = [
        "close",
        "high",
        "low",
        "volume",
        "epsSurprise",
        "revenueSurprise",
        "cashRatio",
        "debtToCapital",
    ]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"].replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        high = data["high"].replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        low = data["low"].replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        volume = data["volume"].replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).fillna(0.0)
        eps = data["epsSurprise"].replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        revenue = data["revenueSurprise"].replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)

        eps_update = _fresh_update(eps)
        revenue_update = _fresh_update(revenue)
        eps_bad = (1.0 - rank(eps)).where(eps_update & eps.lt(0.0), 0.0)
        revenue_bad = (1.0 - rank(revenue)).where(revenue_update & revenue.lt(0.0), 0.0)
        event_count = eps_update.astype(float) + revenue_update.astype(float)
        fresh_bad_news = ((eps_bad + revenue_bad) / event_count.replace(0.0, np.nan))
        fresh_bad_news = fresh_bad_news.fillna(0.0)
        news_state = _decayed_event_state(fresh_bad_news, 4.0)

        cash = data["cashRatio"].clip(lower=0.0)
        debt = data["debtToCapital"].clip(lower=-1.0, upper=2.0)
        fragility = (
            (1.0 - rank(cash).fillna(0.5))
            + rank(debt).fillna(0.5)
        ) / 2.0

        exhaustion = _downside_liquidation_cooling(close, high, low, volume)
        raw_long_score = news_state * fragility * exhaustion
        signal = rank(raw_long_score).fillna(0.0)
        return signal.where(raw_long_score.gt(0.0), 0.0).fillna(0.0)

This child treats a negative disclosure as an information trigger, but goes long only when a clustered downside price-volume liquidation impulse is cooling and the bar closes away from its low, indicating that marginal sellers have been absorbed. The edge should persist because event-driven deleveraging, mandate selling, and liquidity-provider inventory constraints can force immediate sales while arbitrageurs rationally wait for the selling process to stabilize; it is falsified if high-score names do not show more negative initial pressure but higher subsequent six-bar returns than equally bad-news fragile firms without cooling pressure.

"""Industry-residual downside-cluster extinction.

Mechanism: a stock-specific downside-volatility burst can arise from a temporary
self-exciting liquidation episode.  When its residual downside energy cools
rapidly after an unusually large burst, the selling cluster is likely becoming
subcritical, leaving a gradual inventory and liquidity-normalisation rebound.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import rank
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _industry_residual_returns(
    ret: pd.DataFrame, industry: pd.DataFrame
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Remove each day's equal-weight industry return using static labels.

    Industry is static in this feed.  The calculation is cross-sectional within
    each date, so it removes common industry bad-news shocks without using any
    future prices.
    """
    labels = industry.iloc[0]
    residual = pd.DataFrame(np.nan, index=ret.index, columns=ret.columns)

    for group in pd.unique(labels.dropna()):
        cols = labels.index[labels == group]
        if len(cols) == 0:
            continue
        group_ret = ret.loc[:, cols].mean(axis=1)
        residual.loc[:, cols] = ret.loc[:, cols].sub(group_ret, axis=0)

    return residual


def _cluster_extinction_score(
    close: pd.DataFrame, industry: pd.DataFrame
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Causal residual downside-energy burst times its subsequent cooling.

    The historical burst ends at t-1.  Current energy is then compared with
    that burst, making a high value specifically an extinguishing, rather than
    persistent, downside-excitation episode.
    """
    ret = close.pct_change().replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
    idio_ret = _industry_residual_returns(ret, industry)
    downside_energy = idio_ret.clip(upper=0.0).pow(2)

    # Recent excitation is deliberately measured before today so that today's
    # cooling is a distinct state transition rather than a same-bar wick score.
    prior_energy = downside_energy.shift(1).rolling(5, min_periods=4).mean()
    current_energy = downside_energy.rolling(2, min_periods=2).mean()

    # A robust, strictly earlier baseline prevents a normal high-volatility
    # name from being labelled as a shock merely because its level is high.
    baseline = (
        downside_energy.shift(2)
        .rolling(50, min_periods=25)
        .median()
        .replace(0.0, np.nan)
    )

    burst = (prior_energy / baseline - 1.0).clip(lower=0.0, upper=12.0)
    cooling = (1.0 - current_energy / prior_energy.replace(0.0, np.nan)).clip(
        lower=0.0, upper=1.0
    )

    score = np.log1p(burst) * cooling
    return score.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)


@register_factor
class IndustryResidualDownsideClusterExtinction(BaseFactor):
    factor_id = "industry_residual_downside_cluster_extinction"
    name = "Industry-Residual Downside Cluster Extinction"
    category = "volatility"
    description = (
        "Ranks names with an unusually large recent industry-residual downside "
        "semivariance burst whose current downside energy has sharply cooled."
    )
    window_length = 57
    inputs = ["close", "industry"]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        score = _cluster_extinction_score(data["close"], data["industry"])
        return rank(score).fillna(0.0)

programs.trading_idea: A burst of downside variance that is idiosyncratic to a stock rather than shared by its industry is more likely to reflect forced liquidation, dealer-inventory stress, or a temporary local liquidity vacuum than a sector-wide information shock. The child goes long only after that downside-energy burst demonstrably cools, treating declining excitation as evidence that the selling cluster has become subcritical and that the remaining inventory overhang should unwind over the next week. The edge can persist because liquidity providers and constrained sellers adjust inventory gradually, while arbitrageurs cannot immediately distinguish an extinguishing forced-flow episode from genuinely adverse private information. This is falsifiable: high-scoring names should outperform over six bars, whereas names whose residual downside energy remains elevated should not.

"""Fresh downside-event clustering as a proxy for endogenous deleveraging.

Mechanism: a negative, high-participation event that occurs within an unexpectedly
accelerating sequence of similar downside events is interpreted as a self-exciting
liquidation cascade.  The signal is intentionally fresh-event gated: it seeks the
near-term continuation of unresolved execution rather than the slower relaxation of
an already observed liquidity state.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import indneutralize, rank
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _exp_downside_intensity(mark: pd.DataFrame, decay: float) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Causal exponential-kernel event intensity, vectorised across tickers.

    This is the discrete-time Hawkes state recursion I_t = mark_t +
    decay * I_(t-1).  It uses the observed event at t, but no future bar.
    """
    values = mark.fillna(0.0).to_numpy(dtype=float)
    out = np.zeros_like(values, dtype=float)
    state = np.zeros(values.shape[1], dtype=float)
    for t in range(values.shape[0]):
        state = values[t] + decay * state
        out[t] = state
    return pd.DataFrame(out, index=mark.index, columns=mark.columns)


def _downside_hawkes_pressure(
    open_: pd.DataFrame,
    high: pd.DataFrame,
    low: pd.DataFrame,
    close: pd.DataFrame,
    volume: pd.DataFrame,
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Fresh, marked downside-cluster surprise estimated using trailing data only."""
    safe_close = close.replace(0.0, np.nan)
    prior_close = safe_close.shift(1)
    ret = (safe_close / prior_close - 1.0).clip(-0.60, 0.60)

    # Lagged normalization makes the current shock an out-of-sample innovation
    # relative to volatility known before the current bar.
    prior_mean = ret.rolling(40, min_periods=20).mean().shift(1)
    prior_std = ret.rolling(40, min_periods=20).std().shift(1)
    downside_z = ((prior_mean - ret) / prior_std.replace(0.0, np.nan)).clip(-2.0, 6.0)
    downside_excess = (downside_z - 0.50).clip(lower=0.0)

    dollar_volume = (safe_close.abs() * volume.abs()).replace(0.0, np.nan)
    typical_dollar_volume = dollar_volume.rolling(30, min_periods=15).median().shift(1)
    relative_volume = (dollar_volume / typical_dollar_volume.replace(0.0, np.nan)).clip(0.05, 20.0)
    participation_mark = np.sqrt(relative_volume).clip(0.25, 4.0)

    bar_range = (high - low).abs().replace(0.0, np.nan)
    close_location = ((safe_close - low) / bar_range).clip(0.0, 1.0)
    unresolved_fraction = (1.0 - close_location).fillna(0.5).clip(0.0, 1.0)

    # The mark combines abnormal bad news, participation, and failure to recover
    # from the intrabar low.  It is zero for ordinary or positive-return bars.
    mark = (downside_excess * participation_mark * (0.30 + 0.70 * unresolved_fraction)).fillna(0.0)

    fast_intensity = _exp_downside_intensity(mark, 0.78)
    expected_rate = mark.rolling(30, min_periods=15).mean().shift(1)
    cluster_surprise = (
        (fast_intensity - expected_rate)
        / np.sqrt(expected_rate.clip(lower=0.0) + 0.10)
    ).clip(lower=0.0, upper=12.0)

    # A current event gate prevents a stale elevated intensity from becoming a
    # delayed, long-horizon signal; it focuses the factor on immediate execution.
    pressure = (mark * cluster_surprise).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
    return pressure


@register_factor
class DownsideHawkesSurpriseDeleveraging(BaseFactor):
    """Short fresh idiosyncratic downside liquidation cascades."""

    factor_id = "downside_hawkes_surprise_deleveraging"
    name = "Downside Hawkes Surprise Deleveraging"
    category = "microstructure"
    description = (
        "Industry-neutral cross-sectional rank of a fresh marked downside-event "
        "cluster surprise, where event marks combine abnormal negative return, "
        "relative dollar volume, and a close near the daily low."
    )
    window_length = 70
    inputs = ["open", "high", "low", "close", "volume", "industry"]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"]
        pressure = _downside_hawkes_pressure(
            data["open"],
            data["high"],
            data["low"],
            close,
            data["volume"],
        ).fillna(0.0)
        idiosyncratic_pressure = indneutralize(pressure, data["industry"]).fillna(0.0)
        return rank(idiosyncratic_pressure).fillna(0.5).reindex(
            index=close.index, columns=close.columns
        )

Such clusters proxy for endogenous deleveraging: risk-targeting and inventory-constrained participants react to prior declines, creating a short-lived self-exciting sell program that should persist over the next six sessions. The effect should survive arbitrage because trading against it requires supplying liquidity precisely when volatility, adverse-selection risk, and capital constraints are highest; it is falsified if fresh excess downside-event intensity predicts a rebound after controlling for the current return, volume, and industry.

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import rank, returns
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _sector_returns(ret: pd.DataFrame, sector: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Causal equal-weighted same-sector return panel."""
    out = pd.DataFrame(np.nan, index=ret.index, columns=ret.columns, dtype=float)
    labels = sector.reindex(index=ret.index, columns=ret.columns).ffill().bfill()
    for timestamp in ret.index:
        row_ret = ret.loc[timestamp]
        row_labels = labels.loc[timestamp]
        valid = row_ret.notna() & row_labels.notna()
        if valid.any():
            sector_mean = row_ret[valid].groupby(row_labels[valid]).mean()
            out.loc[timestamp, valid] = row_labels[valid].map(sector_mean).astype(float)
    return out


def _excess_downside_beta(
    stock_ret: pd.DataFrame, sector_ret: pd.DataFrame, window: int
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Trailing downside beta minus ordinary beta using only sector-tail days."""
    x_mean = sector_ret.rolling(window, min_periods=window).mean()
    y_mean = stock_ret.rolling(window, min_periods=window).mean()
    xy_mean = (stock_ret * sector_ret).rolling(window, min_periods=window).mean()
    x2_mean = (sector_ret * sector_ret).rolling(window, min_periods=window).mean()
    ordinary = (xy_mean - x_mean * y_mean) / (x2_mean - x_mean * x_mean).replace(0.0, np.nan)

    cutoff = sector_ret.rolling(window, min_periods=window).quantile(0.20)
    tail = sector_ret.le(cutoff) & sector_ret.lt(0.0)
    masked_x = sector_ret.where(tail)
    masked_y = stock_ret.where(tail)
    count = tail.astype(float).rolling(window, min_periods=window).sum()

    tail_x = masked_x.rolling(window, min_periods=1).sum() / count.replace(0.0, np.nan)
    tail_y = masked_y.rolling(window, min_periods=1).sum() / count.replace(0.0, np.nan)
    tail_xy = (masked_x * masked_y).rolling(window, min_periods=1).sum() / count.replace(0.0, np.nan)
    tail_x2 = (masked_x * masked_x).rolling(window, min_periods=1).sum() / count.replace(0.0, np.nan)
    tail_beta = (tail_xy - tail_x * tail_y) / (tail_x2 - tail_x * tail_x).replace(0.0, np.nan)
    return (tail_beta - ordinary).where(count >= 8.0)


def _standardized_innovation(values: pd.DataFrame, window: int) -> pd.DataFrame:
    mean = values.rolling(window, min_periods=window).mean()
    stdev = values.rolling(window, min_periods=window).std().replace(0.0, np.nan)
    return ((values - mean) / stdev).clip(lower=-5.0, upper=5.0).fillna(0.0)


def _fragility(
    cash_ratio: pd.DataFrame,
    debt_to_equity: pd.DataFrame,
    interest_coverage: pd.DataFrame,
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    cash = cash_ratio.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).clip(lower=0.0)
    debt = debt_to_equity.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).clip(lower=0.0)
    coverage = interest_coverage.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).clip(lower=0.0)
    score = (1.0 - rank(cash) + rank(debt) + 1.0 - rank(coverage)) / 3.0
    return score.fillna(0.5)


@register_factor
class SectorTailVolumeBacklogFragility(BaseFactor):
    factor_id = "sector_tail_volume_backlog_fragility"
    name = "Sector Tail-Exposure Volume Backlog"
    category = "microstructure"
    description = (
        "Shorts fragile firms with excess sector downside-tail beta when fresh sector "
        "stress coincides with abnormal volume that follows prior downside-range shocks."
    )
    window_length = 80
    inputs = [
        "close", "high", "low", "volume", "sector", "cashRatio",
        "debtToEquity", "interestCoverage"
    ]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"].replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        high = data["high"].replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        low = data["low"].replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        volume = data["volume"].replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        ret = returns(data).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)

        sector_ret = _sector_returns(ret, data["sector"])
        excess_beta = _excess_downside_beta(ret, sector_ret, 60).clip(lower=0.0)
        sector_vol = sector_ret.rolling(20, min_periods=10).std().replace(0.0, np.nan)
        sector_shock = ((-sector_ret) / sector_vol).clip(lower=0.0, upper=4.0).fillna(0.0)

        previous_close = close.shift(1).replace(0.0, np.nan)
        range_width = (high - low).clip(lower=0.0).replace(0.0, np.nan)
        weak_close = ((high - close).clip(lower=0.0) / range_width).clip(lower=0.0, upper=1.0)
        downside_range = ((previous_close - low).clip(lower=0.0) / previous_close) * weak_close
        downside_z = _standardized_innovation(downside_range, 15)
        volume_z = _standardized_innovation(np.log1p(volume.clip(lower=0.0)), 15)

        delayed_alignment = (volume_z * downside_z.shift(2)).rolling(10, min_periods=8).mean()
        concurrent_alignment = (volume_z * downside_z).rolling(10, min_periods=8).mean()
        backlog = (delayed_alignment - concurrent_alignment).clip(lower=0.0).fillna(0.0)

        fragility = _fragility(
            data["cashRatio"], data["debtToEquity"], data["interestCoverage"]
        )
        liquidation_pressure = backlog * excess_beta.fillna(0.0) * fragility * sector_shock
        signal = rank(-liquidation_pressure).fillna(0.5)
        return signal.reindex(index=close.index, columns=close.columns).astype(float)

Sector-tail exposure and balance-sheet fragility identify names likely to be mechanically de-risked, while the delayed-volume component identifies that the liquidation process is still active rather than already absorbed. Neither parent alone distinguishes financially fragile tail-beta names with an unresolved execution backlog from those whose sector shock has already cleared.

High liquidation pressure is assigned a low score, so the factor is long likely absorbers and short names with unresolved forced-sale backlog.

"""Scheduled-order completion reversal from fading weekly flow footprints.

Mechanism: recurring same-phase pressure can reflect institutional execution,
but the parent factor's negative out-of-sample IC indicates that the relevant
six-bar effect is inventory-release reversal after the schedule fades, rather
than continuation.  The factor therefore trades against a coherent historical
weekly pressure direction only when the current expected execution episode is
substantially weaker than its own previous same-phase episodes.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _prior_weekly_schedule(
    pressure: pd.DataFrame,
    weekly_lag: int = 5,
    cycles: int = 10,
) -> tuple[pd.DataFrame, pd.DataFrame, pd.DataFrame]:
    """Return prior same-phase signed flow, coherence, and mean magnitude.

    All samples are strictly lagged by at least one weekly phase.  Thus the
    schedule estimate at time t contains no current-bar information beyond the
    separately observed current pressure used to identify completion.
    """
    signed_sum = pressure.shift(weekly_lag).fillna(0.0)
    abs_sum = pressure.shift(weekly_lag).abs().fillna(0.0)

    for k in range(2, cycles + 1):
        lagged = pressure.shift(weekly_lag * k)
        signed_sum = signed_sum + lagged.fillna(0.0)
        abs_sum = abs_sum + lagged.abs().fillna(0.0)

    mean_abs = abs_sum / float(cycles)
    coherence = signed_sum.abs() / abs_sum.replace(0.0, np.nan)
    coherence = coherence.clip(lower=0.0, upper=1.0)
    return signed_sum, coherence, mean_abs


@register_factor
class WeeklyScheduleCompletionInventoryReversal(BaseFactor):
    factor_id = "weekly_schedule_completion_inventory_reversal"
    name = "Weekly Schedule Completion Reversal"
    category = "microstructure"
    description = (
        "Reverses the direction of a coherent prior weekly signed-volume "
        "schedule when its current same-phase pressure has faded, indicating "
        "likely parent-order completion and liquidity-provider inventory release."
    )
    window_length = 70
    inputs = ["open", "close", "volume"]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        open_price = data["open"]
        close = data["close"]
        volume = data["volume"]

        bar_direction = np.sign((close - open_price).fillna(0.0))
        log_volume = np.log1p(volume.clip(lower=0.0).fillna(0.0))
        volume_base = log_volume.rolling(20, min_periods=10).mean()
        relative_volume = log_volume / volume_base.replace(0.0, np.nan)
        pressure = (bar_direction * relative_volume).replace(
            [np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan
        ).fillna(0.0)

        scheduled_flow, coherence, prior_magnitude = _prior_weekly_schedule(pressure)

        current_relative_size = pressure.abs() / prior_magnitude.replace(0.0, np.nan)
        completion = (1.0 - current_relative_size).clip(lower=0.0, upper=1.0)

        same_direction = (
            np.sign(pressure) * np.sign(scheduled_flow)
        ).where(lambda x: x > 0.0, 0.0)

        raw_signal = -np.sign(scheduled_flow) * coherence * completion * same_direction
        valid = coherence.notna() & prior_magnitude.notna() & (prior_magnitude > 0.0)
        raw_signal = raw_signal.where(valid, np.nan).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)

        return raw_signal.rank(axis=1, pct=True).fillna(0.5)
